paragraphs: Item 1.01 Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement.

On October 9, 2026, Co-Diagnostics, Inc. (the "Company") entered into a Loan Agreement (the "Loan Agreement") with J.J. Astor & Co. (the "Lender"), pursuant to which the Lender agreed to provide loans to the Company in an aggregate principal funding amount of up to $3.1 million. At the initial closing, the Lender funded an initial loan of $2.1 million and the Company issued to the Lender a senior secured convertible installment promissory note having an original principal amount of $2.835 million (the "Initial Note"). Beginning 60 days after the date of the Loan Agreement, subject to the satisfaction of the conditions set forth in the Loan Agreement, the Company may elect to borrow an additional $1.0 million and issue an additional senior secured convertible installment promissory note having an original principal amount of $1.35 million (the "Additional Note" and, together with the Initial Note, the "Notes"). The original principal amounts of the Notes reflect a factor rate of 1.35 times the applicable funded amount. The Lender retained a 4% origination fee from the initial funded amount, resulting in initial net cash proceeds of approximately $2.016 million before other transaction expenses. Under the terms of the Loan Agreement and the Notes, the Company must maintain a minimum cash balance of $250,000 while the Notes are outstanding. The Company intends to use the net proceeds for general working capital purposes.

The Notes are payable in 30 weekly installments and are secured by a senior-priority lien on substantially all assets of the Company and its existing subsidiaries as subsidiary guarantors pursuant to a pledge and security agreement (the "Pledge and Security Agreement") and a subsidiary guarantee (the "Subsidiary Guarantee"). The Company may prepay a Note at any time without penalty. If a Note is paid in full within 45 days after its funding date and no event of default has occurred, the repayment amount will be reduced to reflect a factor rate of 1.29 times the applicable funded amount, less all weekly installment payments previously made. Upon an event of default, the outstanding balance becomes immediately due and payable, the outstanding principal amount of the Initial Note and (if issued) the Additional Note is increased to 120% of the then-outstanding principal amount(s) and bear default interest at 19% per annum, compounded daily (the "Default Amount") and may be converted by the Lender at the Event of Default Conversion Price (as defined in the Loan Agreement).

In connection with the transaction, the Company issued the Lender 600,000 shares of common stock as commitment shares (the "Commitment Shares") at the closing date, subject to a make-whole provision, which provides that the company will issue make-whole shares if the Commitment Shares are sold on a day when the closing price of the Company's stock is less than $0.218. The Company also agreed to reserve shares for issuance upon conversion of the Notes and to seek stockholder approval for issuances exceeding the applicable Nasdaq issuance limitation.

The Loan Agreement requires the Company to file a preliminary proxy statement within five business days after funding of the Initial Loan, mail the definitive proxy statement within five business days after SEC clearance, and hold the stockholder meeting within 30 days after mailing.

The Company, the Lender and Maxim Group LLC, the Company's sales agent under its existing at-the-market offering program (the "ATM Program"), also entered into an ATM Waterfall Distribution Agreement. Under that agreement, 100% of the net proceeds from sales under the ATM Program, after deduction only of the sales agent's commissions, are to be remitted to a deposit account subject to a deposit account control agreement in favor of the Lender. The initial $1.0 million of such net proceeds is payable to the Lender. Thereafter, 80% of such net proceeds is applied to the Notes and 20% is released to the Company until the required weekly installment payments for the applicable week have been satisfied; for the remainder of that week, 25% is applied to the Notes and 75% is released to the Company. Following an event of default, 80% of such net proceeds is applied to the obligations under the Notes and 20% is released to the Company. Distributions to the Company are further limited if the market value of the registered, freely tradeable shares available under the ATM Program is less than 200% of the outstanding principal amount of the Notes. The ATM Waterfall Distribution Agreement remains in effect until all obligations under the Notes have been paid in full.

The Loan Agreement contains customary representations, warranties, affirmative and negative covenants and events of default, including covenants relating to additional indebtedness and equity issuances, maintenance and use of the ATM Program, maintenance of Nasdaq listing, timely filing of reports under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and maintenance of specified share reserves and ATM availability.

In connection with the transaction, the Company entered into a placement agency agreement (the "Placement Agency Agreement") with Maxim Group LLC ("Maxim"), pursuant to which Maxim agreed to act as the Company's exclusive placement agent on a reasonable best efforts basis in connection with the placement of the Notes. The Company agreed to pay Maxim a cash fee equal to 5.0% of the gross proceeds received by the Company at the initial closing and at any additional closing and to reimburse Maxim for its reasonable expenses, including fees and disbursements of its counsel, up to $5,000. Maxim also is entitled to a transaction fee equal to 5.0% of the proceeds of any public or private financing or other capital-raising transaction consummated during the 12-month period following the closing (or, if no closing occurs, termination of the engagement) with an investor actually contacted or introduced to the Company by Maxim during the term of the Placement Agency Agreement. The engagement continues until the earlier of the final closing of the placement, including any additional closings, and termination by either party upon written notice. The Placement Agency Agreement also contains customary representations, warranties, covenants, closing conditions, indemnification and contribution provisions and other terms and conditions.

The foregoing descriptions of the Loan Agreement, the Notes, the Pledge and Security Agreement, the Subsidiary Guarantee, the ATM Waterfall Distribution Agreement, the Registration Rights Agreement and the Placement Agency Agreement do not purport to be complete and are qualified in their entirety by reference to the full text of such documents, copies of which are filed as exhibits to this Current Report on Form 8-K and are incorporated herein by reference.

The Company issued the Initial Note and the Commitment Shares, and may issue the Additional Note, the Conversion Shares, and any make-whole shares, in reliance on the exemption from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"), provided by Section 4(a)(2) thereof and/or Rule 506(b) of Regulation D promulgated thereunder. The Lender represented that it is an "accredited investor" as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D. Neither the Notes nor the Commitment Shares were, and any Conversion Shares or make-whole shares issued absent registration will not be, registered under the Securities Act and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration.
